message.content: {"decision":"PROPOSE","observations":["All three source tasks ask for the number of distinct values obtainable by fully parenthesizing a fixed sequence of operands and binary operators (+,-,*), preserving order.","The shared interface supplies operands (list of integers) and operators (list of strings, length len(operands)-1).","The mathematical object is the set of results over all binary parse trees of the operator sequence; this is exactly interval dynamic programming over sets of reachable values.","Failures in the evidence are consistent with manual enumeration/estimation errors (truncation, guessing, incomplete DP), not with a flaw in the DP formulation itself.","The DP is deterministic and parameterized only by operands and operators; no semantic routing is needed."],"procedure_plan":"Implement solve(parameters) with operands a[0..n-1] and operators op[0..n-2]. If n==1 return 1 (single value). Build dp[i][j] = set of all values from fully parenthesizing a[i..j]. Base: dp[i][i]={a[i]}. For length L=2..n, for i=0..n-L, j=i+L-1, for split k=i..j-1, combine every x in dp[i][k] and y in dp[k+1][j] via op[k]: '+' -> x+y, '-' -> x-y, '*' -> x*y; add to dp[i][j]. Return the cardinality of dp[0][n-1]. Use Python ints (arbitrary precision); sets deduplicate automatically. Complexity is bounded by Catalan-many combinations but with set deduplication; for n<=8 this is small.","uncertainty":"The DP is standard and exact; the only risk is performance if intermediate sets grow large, but with n<=8 operands and values bounded by products of small integers, sets remain manageable. No correctness uncertainty about the formulation.","invalid_operation":null,"replacement_operation":null}
